content.title: It's the first day of spring 2026. When is the equinox?
content.text: It's officially the first day of spring. The vernal equinox is March 20, which means winter is finally over.Unfortunately, it also means the ants that survived the mild cold season will be out in full force to ruin family picnics and pester people who don't fortify their homes against the little critters.Here's what to know about the first day of spring and the 2026 spring equinox.When is the first day of Spring 2026?The first day of Spring 2026 is Friday, March 20.What is the spring equinox?The spring equinox marks the exact moment the center of the sun crosses Earth's equator, meaning a person could see the sun directly overhead at noon if they were standing on the equator, according to NASA.After the March equinox, the sun's path continues shifting north each day until it reaches its northernmost point during the June solstice. It then begins moving south again, crossing the equator during the September equinox before continuing south to the December solstice.At the March equinox, the Northern Hemisphere will begin moving into spring, while the Southern Hemisphere heads into fall.An amazing view of the Earth at the spring equinox was taken in 2013 by NOAA's GOES-13 satellite.What does vernal equinox mean?The vernal equinox is the name for the spring equinox in the Northern Hemisphere.It is one of two equinoxes that occur each year. During these events, Earth's equator is not tilted toward or away from the sun, resulting in nearly equal lengths of day and night across all latitudes, according to the National Weather Service.The equinox that occurs in spring is called the vernal equinox, while the one in fall is called the autumnal equinox.Why do days get longer in spring?The days grow longer throughout spring because the Northern Hemisphere gradually tilts more toward the sun.It continues to tilt until it reaches its maximum point during the summer solstice, known as the longest day of the year.When is daylight saving time 2026?Oregonians will need to spring their clocks forward for daylight saving time on Sunday, March 8.Ginnie Sandoval is the Oregon Connect reporter for the Statesman Journal. Sandoval can be reached at GSandoval@statesmanjournal.com or on X at @GinnieSandoval.This article originally appeared on Salem Statesman Journal: Spring has sprung in Oregon. When is the equinox?
